description.narrative:
Increased access to finance for MSMEs, including women borrowers: The proposed investment will increase access to finance for the underbanked and credit-starved MSMEs, including women borrowers, thereby enabling them to expand their business, generate income, and, thus, contribute to their economic empowerment.
Competitiveness: IFC anticipates that the Project will promote greater competitiveness in the NBFC sector by encouraging NBFCs to grow their MSME portfolios, especially to underserved, harder-to-reach segments like WMSMEs in small towns and rural areas.

The proposed project envisages an investment of up to US$50 million in SBFC Finance Limited (SBFC or the Company), an Indian Non-Banking Finance Company (NBFC) and a new client for IFC (the Project). IFCs debt proceeds will be utilized by the Company for growing its loan book towards micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSME), including women MSMEs. A portion of IFCs investment proceeds will also be utilized by the Company for financing the targeted borrower groups in the state of Uttar Pradesh.
